name: Lordship of Ireland
alt: Lordship of Ireland under the English Crown

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Leinster
predecessors.text: Leinster, granted to Strongbow as a fiefdom (1171 section of the Lordship article)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Meath
predecessors.text: the 'unconquered kingdom of Meath' granted to Hugh de Lacy; royal troops entered Meath in early 1172

predecessors.name: Ulaid
predecessors.text: Ulaid east of the Bann, conquered by John de Courcy from February 1177

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Connacht
predecessors.text: Connacht, conquered 1235 by Richard Mor de Burgh, who held 25 cantreds in chief of the Crown

predecessors.name: Airgíalla
predecessors.text: Louth, the 'Uriel' of the Anglo-Normans: 'The Normans occupied the Louth area in the 1180s, forming the County of Oriel (Uriel or Vriell)'

successors.name: Kingdom of Ireland
successors.text: the Pale, the only part directly ruled from Dublin; the title became King of Ireland by the Crown of Ireland Act (18 June 1542) and the claim covered the whole island

ledger.x: 1171: Henry II lands at Waterford and the Norman conquests become a Crown lordship.
1171: Henry II grants Leinster to Strongbow as a fiefdom.
1176: Domhnall Mor Ua Briain retakes Limerick.
1177: the Council of Oxford grants Desmond to FitzStephen and de Cogan and makes John 'Lord of Ireland'.
1177: John de Courcy conquers east Ulaid.
1235: Richard Mor de Burgh conquers Connacht.
1235: the Ua Conchobair king becomes the de Burgh lord's vassal.
1318: Bruce defeated and the invasion ends.
1333: the murder of the 3rd Earl of Ulster.
ledger.cp: Gaelic and Burke lords of Connacht and Ulster

ledger.x: 1348: the Black Death and the shrinking to the Pale.
1361: the capital moves to Carlow until 1394.

1375: Art MacMurrough-Kavanagh begins to reign ('ruled from 1375 to 1417'); the kingdom 'continued to control much of what is today County Wexford and County Carlow' and parts of Wicklow until the early 17th century (Kingdom of Leinster page).
1394: the capital returns to Dublin (end of the Carlow span in the infobox).
1474: the last Ua Conchobair king dies.
1542: the Lordship becomes the Kingdom of Ireland.

wars.name: Norman invasion of Ireland
wars.outcome: Normans take Waterford, Dublin (1170), Leinster and Meath; Henry II lands October 1171; Treaty of Windsor 6 October 1175; de Courcy takes Downpatrick February 1177; John made Lord of Ireland 1177.

wars.name: Bruce campaign in Ireland
wars.outcome: Edward Bruce defeated at Faughart near Dundalk; the economy of the Lordship was destroyed.

wars.name: Kildare Rebellion
wars.outcome: A failed rebellion; it 'served in the following decades to hasten the Tudor conquest of Ireland'.

certainty.note: The Lordship's extent is never described by a boundary in the pages; the English-held area is a patchwork of lordships, then the Pale (a ditch from 1494 only around parts of Louth, Meath, Dublin and Kildare).

sources.title: Richard Mor de Burgh, 1st Baron of Connaught
